extracted.intended_audience: policy-makers, regulators, legal advisers and managers of public service broadcasters; UNESCO/AIBD participants
extracted.subtask_description: Legal and normative standards for organising, funding, governing, and operating national public service broadcasting organisations to ensure editorial independence, pluralism, accountability and adequate public service programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: General geographical availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Public service should be available across the whole territory; not appropriate to offer the public service to only part of the population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first feature: 'general geographical availability'—the public’s right to know should be satisfied in equal measure throughout the whole territory, though different regions may receive different services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concern for national identity and culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Public service broadcasters have obligations relating to national identity, culture and promotion of a democratic, rights-respecting culture, including multiculturalism as part of nationhood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The role includes building a sense of national identity, belonging and participation; recognized as an explicit obligation in many countries but must be balanced to avoid chauvinism and not unduly restrict editorial freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence from State and commercial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Public service broadcasters should be independent of both the State and commercial interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence is necessary to avoid government or commercial control that would undermine editorial independence and the public interest; structures must minimise risk of interference (e.g., independent governing boards, financial safeguards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality of programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmes should be impartial and not promote a particular political party or viewpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impartiality is closely related to independence; public funding should not be used to promote the government’s viewpoint and PSB must not promote a specific political position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range and variety of programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: PSBs should provide a variety of programmes including informational, educational and entertainment content, serving diverse interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversity in programming derives from the public’s right to know and ensures access to information on a wide variety of issues; obligation to include programmes not driven solely by market forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial public financing (typical: user charge/license fee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public service broadcasting is often (but not always) substantially financed by a general charge on users (license fee) or public appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License fees are more stable and less susceptible to political interference but difficult to introduce; parliamentary appropriations are common; funding method should aim to protect editorial and institutional autonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee of freedom of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: State obligations under international instruments (UDHR, ICCPR, regional conventions) apply to state-funded broadcasters and require respect for freedom of expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because state-funded broadcasters are linked to the State, guarantees of freedom of expression apply with particular force and the State must adopt measures to give effect to these rights, including positive steps to promote pluralism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of pluralism and equal access
rubrics_metrics.description: States must promote pluralism in media and ensure equal access so that communication media are potentially open to all without discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PSBs make an important contribution to pluralism; international jurisprudence and instruments stress the need for variety and access to a multiplicity of sources as part of freedom of expression obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent governing/supervisory bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Powers of supervisory or governing bodies should be clearly set out in legislation and these bodies must be independent and not have the right to interfere with programming matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation R(96)10: governing bodies should be established to minimise interference (open appointments, guarantees against dismissal, conflict-of-interest rules); statutory clarity of powers is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial independence guaranteed by law
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle of editorial independence should be guaranteed by law; management should be responsible for day-to-day editorial decisions while supervisory bodies set overall policy but do not interfere with programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation between governing body and managers/editors is critical; governing bodies may set directions and policy but should refrain from intervening in editorial matters except in extreme situations; news should present facts fairly and encourage free opinion-formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure, appropriate and transparent funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding must be appropriate to PSB tasks, secure, transparent and protect broadcasters from arbitrary interference with budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles 17-19 of R(96)10 and ARTICLE 19 Recommendation 3: funding arrangements should not render broadcasters susceptible to political interference; transparency and sufficiency are essential so PSBs can fulfil mandates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of commercial dependency; limits on commercial activity
rubrics_metrics.description: PSBs should avoid reliance solely on commercial revenue; some commercial activities may be allowed but with limits to preserve public service remit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial dependency risks programming based on popularity tests; a balance (blended public and commercial revenue with emphasis on the former) is recommended. Advertising and spin-off industries can supplement but must not dominate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accountability and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: PSBs must be accountable to the public via mechanisms such as annual reports, parliamentary reporting, external audits and the ability of Parliament to question board members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards typically present annual reports including full financial accounting and information on how mandates were fulfilled; Parliament may call boards to account. Accountability should supplement, not replace, editorial independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaints procedures and adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms for public complaints should exist (internal review, independent standards agencies), with a carefully delineated scope excluding mere disagreement over editorial perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complaints processes should allow review internally and by neutral third parties; scope should focus on failures to fulfil stated aims/obligations (e.g., Australia) rather than political complaints; regulators may compel remedies when internal processes fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultative/advisory bodies for audience input
rubrics_metrics.description: Permanent or ad hoc consultative bodies should advise PSBs on audience needs, including regional and minority representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If carefully constituted and shielded from political appointments, consultative bodies (regional, minority, or topical) can provide constructive non-coercive mechanisms of accountability and keep boards in touch with public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pluralistic, open appointment processes for boards
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment processes should involve a range of individuals representing significant political viewpoints and allow civil society input to avoid partisan nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical to board independence: open appointments, criteria for expertise, prohibitions on political figures or convicted persons, conflict-of-interest rules, representativeness, guaranteed security of tenure, and non-politicised remuneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security of tenure and protection against political retaliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Board members and key staff should have secure tenure and protection from arbitrary dismissal to prevent self-censorship and political manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security of tenure and stable remuneration help insulate governance from political pressure; removal/amendment processes should be constrained and transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear legal remit and public service mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: PSBs should have a clearly defined public service mandate set out in law and/or charters specifying obligations, services, and programming duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Country sections are organised to show Public Service Mandate (legal and administrative obligations); mandates may require certain programme quotas, minority-language services, or channels serving distinct functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of regulatory licensing from political control
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing procedures must be governed by freedom of expression guarantees and should not be used as a vehicle for government control over broadcasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing restrictions are subject to strict legal tests; regulators and licensing bodies must be independent and licensing should not become a means for surreptitious censorship on technical grounds; where licensing is non-formal it should be guaranteed by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency in funding and budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding mechanisms and budgetary allocations should be transparent to ensure public trust and reduce opportunities for political manipulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reports and externally audited accounts should make funding and spending transparent; processes for setting license-fee rates or parliamentary appropriations should be clear and public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for services to minorities and culturally diverse audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: PSBs should provide specialised services for minority and culturally diverse populations (e.g., SBS model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming obligations and specialised channels may be required to meet the media needs of culturally diverse populations; independent producers and community broadcasters can also receive public funding to serve these needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for independent production and inclusion of independent producers
rubrics_metrics.description: PSBs may be required to include a certain proportion of programmes from independent producers and/or support independent production through funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including independent producers helps diversify content beyond in-house production; some jurisdictions require PSBs to source programming from independent producers as part of the public service remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms to keep PSBs connected with public opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards should use polls, surveys, seminars, public meetings and advisory bodies to remain responsive to public needs and perceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal and informal mechanisms (civil society actors, consumer groups, media organizations) provide oversight and publicity is a critical tool since PSBs depend on public support for funding and existence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection against using PSB to promote government propaganda (prevent State broadcasting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal and institutional safeguards must prevent state-funded broadcasters from becoming mouthpieces for the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have emphasized that state-owned media are national assets belonging to the community, not the government; laws, independent boards and editorial safeguards are required to prevent governmental misuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate balance between public service objectives and efficiency/modern challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: PSBs should adapt to technological and market changes while preserving public service objectives (quality, diversity, independence) and not be forced to mimic commercial broadcasters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital proliferation, satellite, cable and internet pose challenges; funding austerity and commercial pressures risk lowering quality. PSBs may adopt blended funding and limited commercial activities but must retain emphasis on public service rather than popularity-driven content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on legitimate grounds for complaints and adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope for upholding complaints should be carefully delimited to exclude disagreements over editorial perspective, focusing instead on failures to meet stated aims and obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Australian system—complaints may be upheld only if they pertain to broadcaster’s failure to fulfil its own stated aims and obligations; independent authorities can compel remedies if internal systems fail.
